# Design System UI — llms.txt
# Agent instruction layer. This file is served at /llms.txt on every page so
# that terminal agents and in-page bots can operate the system without a human.

## What this is
A single-page workflow builder. A bot or human designs a ComfyUI-style node
graph, executes it in an isolated backend, and a Gemma 4 12B evaluator scores
the result and decides "iterate" or "done". Every capability below is reachable
by HTTP — no page navigation, no browser required.

## Base URL
Default: http://localhost:8000

## Actions (HTTP API)
GET  /                          -> the single-page UI (HTML)
GET  /llms.txt                  -> this file
GET  /health                    -> {status, service, timestamp}
GET  /api/patterns              -> {patterns: {id: {name, description, icon}}}
GET  /api/integrations          -> honest capability manifest: builtin / adapter_ready / unverified_roadmap
GET  /api/stock/status          -> stock providers + whether each is connected
GET  /api/agent/activity?since=N -> {active, events[], latest_seq} activity feed
POST /api/workflow/execute      -> run a workflow, returns {status, output, results, timestamp}
POST /api/workflow/evaluate     -> Gemma 4 12B scoring, returns {score, feedback, suggestions, verdict}
POST /api/workflow/suggest-params -> {model, temperature, ...} for a node type
POST /api/agent/activity        -> broadcast what you are doing (see protocol below)
POST /api/chat                  -> {message, history[]} -> {reply, model, live}
POST /api/stock/search          -> {provider, query, per_page} -> provider results

## Agent visibility protocol (MANDATORY for agents driving this UI)
Humans must be able to SEE when an AI is working. While you operate the
system, POST /api/agent/activity with:

  {"actor":  "<your name, e.g. claude|gpt|deepseek|opencode|pi|playwright>",
   "action": "click|type|execute|evaluate|session-start|session-end|work",
   "target": "<CSS selector or workflow node id you are acting on>",
   "detail": "<short human-readable description>",
   "state":  "working|done|error"}

Effects in the UI (polled every second):
  - state=working within the last ~6s -> red glow around the whole monitor
    edge (body.agent-active) + activity ticker "KI arbeitet: <actor> ...".
  - target that matches a DOM selector -> that element flashes red twice.
  - target that matches a workflow node id -> the canvas flashes.
  - state=done on your last event -> glow fades out.

Protocol rules:
  1. POST action=session-start before your first UI operation.
  2. POST one event per meaningful step (a click, an execution, a read).
  3. POST state=done (action=session-end) when finished; state=error on abort.
  4. In-page agents may call window.agentActivity.click(sel, detail) /
     .start() / .stop() instead of raw fetches — same protocol.

A complete reference implementation is demo/agent_demo.mjs (Playwright): it
loads a template, executes, reads the verdict — every step broadcast, with
screenshots. Run: cd demo && npm install playwright &&
CHROMIUM_PATH=<chromium> node agent_demo.mjs http://localhost:8000 ./shots

## Chat (in-UI assistant, also usable headless)
POST /api/chat {"message": "...", "history": [{"role":"user|assistant","content":"..."}]}
-> {"reply": "...", "model": "gemma:12b"|"heuristic", "live": true|false}
live=true when Ollama answers; false -> static offline help, same schema.

## Stock media (1-click connect)
A provider is connected the moment its env var is set — nothing else:
  PEXELS_API_KEY       -> pexels   (photos+videos)
  UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY  -> unsplash (photos)
  PIXABAY_API_KEY      -> pixabay  (photos+videos)
Check GET /api/stock/status, then POST /api/stock/search
{"provider":"pexels","query":"studio background","per_page":10}.
Responses are passed through verbatim from the provider API.

## Integration surface for other ecosystems
Everything above is plain HTTP+JSON — no SDK. That is the deliberate
interface for Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, opencode, pi-agent, OpenManus,
OpenHands, browser-use etc.: read this file, then call the endpoints.
GET /api/integrations tells you honestly which integrations are built in,
which are adapter-ready patterns, and which remain unverified roadmap names.
On-demand pattern for heavy agent frameworks: keep them OFF until a task
arrives, run them against this API, broadcast via the activity protocol,
shut them down (see README "On-demand agents").

## Workflow object (request body for /api/workflow/execute)
{
  "id": "workflow-123",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "in1",  "type": "text-input",  "x": 100, "y": 100, "params": {}},
    {"id": "llm1", "type": "llm-node",    "x": 300, "y": 100,
       "params": {"model": "gemma-4", "temperature": 0.7}},
    {"id": "out1", "type": "text-output", "x": 500, "y": 100, "params": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"from": "in1", "to": "llm1"},
    {"from": "llm1", "to": "out1"}
  ],
  "parameters": {}
}

## Node types
input:      text-input, file-input, image-input   (id must end in "input")
processing: llm-node, transform, filter
output:     text-output, file-output              (id must end in "output")

A valid workflow needs at least one input node and one output node.

## Evaluate response and the iterate loop
/api/workflow/evaluate returns:
  {"score": 0-100, "feedback": "...", "suggestions": [...],
   "verdict": "iterate" | "done", "model": "gemma:12b",
   "gemma_live": true|false}

gemma_live=true means a real Gemma model (via Ollama) wrote the critique;
false means the deterministic heuristic evaluator answered (Ollama not
running). Both modes return the same schema — agents need no special casing.

Recommended agent loop:
  1. Build or LOAD a pattern (GET /api/patterns for the catalog).
  2. POST /api/workflow/execute.
  3. POST /api/workflow/evaluate with {workflow, results}.
  4. If verdict == "iterate": apply suggestions[].action, go to step 2.
     If verdict == "done": stop and report score + feedback.

## Patterns (starting templates)
text-classifier, rag-pipeline, agent-loop, eval-loop
Fetch metadata via GET /api/patterns; load node layouts client-side or
construct the equivalent nodes/edges from the shapes documented above.

## curl examples
curl http://localhost:8000/api/patterns
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/workflow/execute \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"wf1","nodes":[{"id":"in1","type":"text-input","x":0,"y":0,"params":{}},{"id":"out1","type":"text-output","x":100,"y":0,"params":{}}],"edges":[{"from":"in1","to":"out1"}]}'

## Going live with real Gemma (zero code changes)
Start Ollama with a Gemma model and the evaluator switches to live inference
automatically (falls back to the heuristic when unreachable):

  ollama pull gemma:12b && ollama serve

Environment overrides:
  OLLAMA_URL     backend URL   (default http://localhost:11434)
  GEMMA_MODEL    model name    (default gemma:12b)
  GEMMA_TIMEOUT  seconds       (default 60)

## Self-test
Run ./test.sh — boots the server on a scratch port and asserts every endpoint,
the iterate loop, and the Go + Rust clients (22 checks).
